prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0046: With the transition from a Mars transit DRM to a shorter duration cis-lunar DRM, data were extracted from an IMM run previously requested for another task (IMM Service Request number 201710623-384; IMM version 4.1, programmed in MatLab® version 8.3 (2014a, MathWorks, Natick, MA)), which included four crew (all male) and excluded EVA conditions for a cis-lunar mission lasting 42 days.
U0047: While a mixed-sex crew is preferable, this run was selected to demonstrate the process while limiting cost and schedule impacts and comes with recognized limitations to the outcomes. 2.1 Scoring Variables The medical conditions were provided to ExMC medical professionals for review.
U0048: These medical professionals included an Aerospace-trained pharmacist and six physicians with training and certification in Aerospace Medicine, Emergency Medicine, Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, and Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, as well as familiarity and experience in operational aerospace medicine practice and the exploration mission concept.
U0049: For the initial version of the medical list, each provider reviewed the conditions and Best/Worst Case scenarios, identifying whether management of each condition or scenario would be feasible for an exploration medical capability specific to the Mars transit Design Reference Mission.
U0050: Specifically, each provider was asked to score the condition based on complexity (low, medium, high) and futility (low, medium, high) as defined in the tables below.
U0051: These scores were translated to a logarithmic scale to roughly estimate the likelihood of successful intervention and good clinical outcome.
U0052: Table 1 shows the definitions and scoring schema assigned to the Complexity category.
U0053: Table 2 shows the definitions and scoring schema assigned to the Futility category.
U0054: Table 1: Complexity variable definition and scoring schema.
U0055: Clinical subject matter experts assigned scores on a logarithmic scale.
U0056: Complexity Key Score Clinical Definition High 1 Large number of resources required to diagnose and treat, or difficult management.
U0057: (i.e.
U0058: Worst Case sepsis) Medium 0.1 Moderate number of resources required Low 0.01 Small number of resources required (i.e.
U0059: Best Case mild headache) Table 2: Futility variable definition and scoring schema.
U0060: Clinical subject matter experts assigned scores on a logarithmic scale.
U0061: Futility Key Score Clinical Definition High 1 Highly likely to result in death or disability despite treatment Medium 0.1 Somewhat likely to result in death or disability despite treatment Low 0.01 Unlikely to result in death or disability The logarithmic score for futility was multiplied by the score for complexity, with the product then divided by the probability of occurrence to provide a final comparative ratio, the Exclusion Score (ES). 𝐸𝑥𝑐𝑙𝑢𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑆𝑐𝑜𝑟𝑒= 𝐶𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑙𝑒𝑥𝑖𝑡𝑦∗𝐹𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑃𝑟𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦 By this schema, conditions that are unlikely to occur (probability), are unlikely to have a good outcome despite full treatment (futility), and are difficult to accommodate in light of resource and training constraints (complexity) will have a high ES.
U0062: Those conditions that are likely to occur, have good expected outcomes, and require minimal resources will have a low ES.
U0063: This allowed for a logical mathematical comparison of the viability of planning for conditions given a resource-limited exploration medical capability.
U0064: It should be noted that, while the probability of occurrence is an evidence-based output from the IMM, the other two variables are subjective clinical SME assessments and logarithmic scores according to the definitions above.
U0065: This is an acknowledged limitation to the methodology of this study and is discussed further in the Limitations and the Future Directions sections below.
U0066: For process purposes, consistent use of the same definition set and scoring algorithm allows for a repeatable process despite these limitations. 2.2 Manual Review Calculated ESs were reviewed by the Exploration Medical Capability Element Scientist (the individual responsible for guiding the science and research of ExMC) to assess any inconsistencies and determine face validity.
U0067: The Element Scientist assessed each condition, considering whether to recommend “Should Plan to Treat” or “Should Not Plan to Treat” based upon the variables (probability, complexity, and futility), the ES, and clinical experience.
